target_customer: Patients with late stage or acute liver disease, with an initial focus on alcohol related hepatitis; paid for by health systems if approved
problem: Liver transplant is the only cure for end stage liver disease and donor organs are scarce. HepaTx develops off the shelf cell therapies delivered by infusion.
business_model: Biotech developing a cell therapy, funded by equity and grants, with no product revenue
product_category: Regenerative medicine, cell therapy for liver disease

founders.name: Eric Schuur
founders.background_notes: Listed as Founder/CEO on the YC page and as CEO in company press releases (2023, 2024). No background found.

competitors.name: Vital Therapies (ELAD system)
competitors.what: Extracorporeal bioartificial liver using human liver cell line cartridges for acute liver failure and alcoholic hepatitis
competitors.traction_then: In clinical trials; a Cedars-Sinai study of ELAD was reported in 2014

technical_complexity.rationale: Developing an off the shelf stem cell derived therapy for liver failure requires cell manufacturing at scale, preclinical proof and regulatory clinical trials.

defensibility.rationale: Licensed Mayo Clinic technology (2024) and clinical regulatory path create barriers, but patent strength and data were not found.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent acquiring or copying the approach; the ELAD trial in alcoholic hepatitis missed its survival endpoint per a research summary.

market_need_then: The company states the market for late stage liver disease is underserved and cost intensive (2023 press release). No 2018 dated figures were found.

branding.domain_note: Uses hepatx.com, the exact name as .com; history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Clinical; tagline Replacing organ transplant with an infusion on YC, Off-the-shelf cell therapies for liver disease on its site

branding.brand_signature: Replacing organ transplant with an infusion

brand_strength.rationale: Inconsistent capitalization (HepatX, HepaTx, Hepatx) across sources and little press about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: HepaTx has stayed a very small preclinical company since YC Summer 2018, with four people listed by YC. It added a scientific advisor in April 2023, licensed adipose derived stem cell technology from Mayo Clinic in September 2024 to move toward human trials focused on alcohol related hepatitis, and its site shows an equity crowdfunding raise. Funding data is thin and conflicting, so progress cannot be judged beyond slow, capital light development.
notes: Funding: CB Insights $120K, Caplight $475K, Wellfound $3.5M and Village $2.1M conflict, and a May 2025 grant appears only on aggregators; all unverified, so no rounds recorded. HQ differs: YC says Bend, Oregon, the company site and press releases say Palo Alto. Site mentions a Wefunder raise and logos for GSVP, Nahkoda VC, StartX and Y Combinator without roles. The ELAD competitor is dated by a 2014 news item; the Nov 2018 study noted in search results is after the batch. Outcome search found no shutdown or acquisition. Completeness pass: the May 2025 grant (Caplight) and an April 2024 round (CB Insights) are recorded without amounts because totals conflict (CB Insights 120K, Caplight 475K, Village 2.1M, PitchBook 6.96M); each round rests on a single database. An NIH SBIR grant press release exists on BioSpace but gives no amount in the results seen.
